record.paper_title: Some open questions in TDDFT: Clues from Lattice Models and Kadanoff-Baym Dynamics
record.original_question: What are the physical regimes and corrective principles for Kadanoff-Baym dynamics combined with many-body perturbation theory when conserving approximations still show fundamental failures, such as breakdown at strong interaction, artificial correlation-induced damping, questionable steady states in extended systems, and violations of positivity in two-particle correlation functions? The setting is the nonequilibrium Green's-function approach, where the Kadanoff-Baym equations use a self-energy from approximations such as second Born, GW, or T-matrix, which conserve macroscopic quantities but do not guarantee all physically required properties.

evidence.quote: All these approximations are conserving [40], i.e. the macroscopic conservation laws (for the energy, the number of particles, etc.) hold, which is a key requirement for time dynamics. The fact that the approximations are conserving does, however, not guarantee the soundness of other important features, as shown in the next Section.

On the more fundamental side, the NEG approach within MBPT manifests other undesirable traits, for example perturbation schemes may break down for strong interactions. However, even for converging schemes, unphysical features can emerge, which can sometimes play an important role.

Moreover, in the KBE-based time dynamics, the MBA:s introduce an artificial correlation induced damping which, in some cases, can completely dominate the evolution. For finite systems, such damped dynamics results in a steady (i.e. never decaying) state. In extended systems, a similar behavior is observed, but with a difference, namely arbitrarily long-lived states occur which, however, eventually decay into a unique steady state. This behavior is certainly artificial in finite systems, while its physical soundness in extended systems is much harder to establish.
However, within conserving MBA:s, correlation functions may violate important properties such as positiveness [117].

artifact.category_tag: Kadanoff-Baym equations and conserving many-body approximations
artifact.status_search_result: No comprehensive resolution is available. Recent works (e.g., 2023 results on the failure of the Baym-Kadanoff construction to match quantum dynamics with thermodynamic critical behavior, and ongoing studies of KBE for open quantum systems) confirm that the listed pathologies of conserving MBA-based KBE remain active research issues, with only partial remedies known in specific regimes. The general problem of jointly curing strong-coupling breakdown, artificial damping, spurious steady states, and positivity violations appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Failure of the Baym-Kadanoff construction to match consistently quantum dynamics with thermodynamic critical behavior
status_evidence.snippet: There is a serious deficiency of the Baym-Kadanoff construction of thermodynamically consistent conserving approximations.
status_evidence.claim: Documents continuing fundamental deficiencies of conserving Baym-Kadanoff approximations.

status_evidence.title: Open Quantum Systems with Kadanoff-Baym Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Solving the Kadanoff-Baym equations is computationally demanding, and approximations, such as conserving self energies, must often be employed.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that conserving self-energy approximations are still required and remain an area of active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Adaptive numerical solution of Kadanoff-Baym equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of correlation-induced damping and steady-state behavior in KBE simulations.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that artificial damping and steady-state issues in KBE persist as numerical/physical concerns.
